newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Gujral to face test vote on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: India's Gujral to face test vote on Tuesday.

text.p: Indian prime minister-designate Inder Kumar Gujral will face a vote of confidence in the lower house of parliament on Tuesday at 11 a.m. (0530 GMT), a senior parliamentary official said.
Gujral, 77, was set to be sworn in as India's 12th prime minister on Monday at 10 a.m. (0430 GMT) at the head of a centre-left government supported by the Congress party.

President Shankar Dayal Sharma appointed Gujral as prime minister late on Sunday after his 15-party United Front coalition and Congress agreed to establish a joint committee to try to strengthen communication between the two formations and ensure a more stable government.

The parliamentary official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters by telephone that the lower house, the Lok Sabha, would convene at 11 a.m. (0530 GMT) on Monday and quickly adjourn after paying tribute to veteran political leader Biju Patnaik, who died last week.
Representatives of all political parties will meet Speaker P.A. Sangma later on Monday to decide when parliament will take up the budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year that began on April 1.

Parliament had been scheduled to discuss the budget this week, but it was not clear whether the formation of a new government would delay consideration of the tax and spending plan which sparked a stock market rally after it was introduced in February.
